why: Tatoeba is attribution-only and its CC0 subset is 2,266 bytes for Spanish against 313,297 for French, so three of the four v1 languages cannot avoid the credits screen. A licence that requires attribution with no reachable credit is a licence violation, which makes this a build gate and not a UI nicety.
surface: S152, reachable from the report sheet S045 and About S137. S152 is NOT in deep/00-PRODUCT-MAP.md, which stops at S151; the map owes a row before P4 renders it.

cases.why: The clean case. Five Tatoeba sentences, one authored sentence, an Apache-2.0 voice that needs no credit, and the CC BY-SA-4.0 frequency list the unit ordering is derived from. Three credits, three kinds covered.
EC-PACK-56 itself: a shipped sentence from an attribution-requiring corpus whose owner string is empty. The build fails; nothing is written.
violations: sentence aaaaaaaaaaaaaaa2 is CC-BY-2.0-FR (attribution required) and names no owner
credits row tatoeba (CC-BY-2.0-FR) renders no owner

cases.why: A voice whose engine nobody declared. Review R7: Piper is GPL-3.0 code whose one Japanese voice is CC BY-NC-SA, so a voice licence is never inherited from its engine — an unknown one requires attribution and has no owner, and must stop the build rather than ship uncredited.
violations: voice clip cccccccccccccc02 (azure/v1) is NOASSERTION (attribution required) and names no owner
credits row voice:azure (NOASSERTION) renders no owner

cases.why: A derived list that is share-alike and has no owner recorded. The frequency ordering reaches the learner as the order the units are taught in; it is neither a sentence nor a voice and has no row of its own anywhere else, which is how it gets forgotten.
violations: credits row hermitdave (CC-BY-SA-4.0) renders no owner
derived list hermitdave is CC-BY-SA-4.0 (attribution required) and names no owner

cases.why: A licence row that simply OMITS `attribution_required`. This used to default to False in the derived-list walk while `licence_for_source` defaulted to True, so a frequency ordering whose row lost one flag produced neither a credit nor a violation. An undeclared licence question must stop the build, never pass it.
violations: credits row hermitdave (CC-BY-SA-4.0) renders no owner
derived list hermitdave is CC-BY-SA-4.0 (attribution required) and names no owner

cases.why: CEFRLex is `oracle_only` — its own text never ships — but the BAND it produces is written onto every `lexeme` row of the pack, so something derived from it does ship. The derived-list walk used to filter on `verdict`, which dropped exactly this row: an NC share-alike source credited nowhere, in a pack whose whole licence story is that the NC data is allowed because the pack is NC.
violations: credits row cefrlex (CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0) renders no owner
derived list cefrlex is CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 (attribution required) and names no owner

note: `violations` is the EXACT set of lines the gate must produce, not a count: one ownerless asset produces two facts (the asset, and the credits row that would render blank), and a test that only counted them would pass on either one alone.
